problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}⟩,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨t-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)⟩,\,t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))⟩ \\  & =⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =0 \\ ⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t=0\, & ⇒\,t=0, \\ -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t=0\, & ⇒\,t=0,\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $t=0$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only value of $t$ when the object is stationary.
